   514→class AppTestScenario:
   515→    """One-call E2E test setup.
   516→
   517→    Automates all boilerplate: TmuxManager, signup/login, create_space,
   518→    connect/publish, add_viewer, open_app, wait for readiness.
   519→
   520→    Usage:
   521→        args = AppTestScenario.parse_args("My test")
   522→        with AppTestScenario(
   523→            name="my_test",
   524→            app_path="sample_apps/my-shop",
   525→            peers={
   526→                "owner":    {"role": "owner",  "app": "Shop Owner"},
   527→                "customer": {"role": "viewer", "app": "Shop Customer"},
   528→            },
   529→            **args,
   530→        ) as s:
   531→            owner = s.peer("owner")
   532→            customer = s.peer("customer")
   533→            owner.eval('add_product_via_ui("Widget", 99, "Test", 50)')
   534→            customer.wait_for(
   535→                lambda: customer.eval("return get_products_count()") >= 1,
   536→                desc="product sync",
   537→            )
   538→    """
   539→
   540→    def __init__(
   541→        self,
   542→        name: str,
   543→        app_path: str,
   544→        peers: Dict[str, Dict[str, str]],
   545→        base_dir: Optional[str] = None,
   546→        release: bool = False,
   547→        profiling: bool = False,
   548→        flame_only: bool = False,
   549→        heaptrack: bool = False,
   550→        keep: bool = False,
   551→        debug: bool = False,
   552→    ):
   553→        """
   554→        Args:
   555→            name: Session name (tmux session + base dir name)
   556→            app_path: Path to the app directory (e.g., sample_apps/my-shop)
   557→            peers: Dict mapping peer name to {"role": "owner"|"viewer", "app": "App Name"}
   558→                   First peer with role "owner" creates the space.
   559→            base_dir: Override base dir (default: /tmp/{name})
   560→            release: Use release builds
   561→            profiling: Enable tokio-console + flame profiling
   562→            flame_only: Enable flame graphs only (no tokio-console overhead)
   563→            heaptrack: Wrap binaries with heaptrack for heap profiling
   564→            keep: Keep session alive after test (block until Ctrl+C)
   565→            debug: Keep session on failure for debugging
   566→        """
   567→        self.name = name
   568→        self.app_path = str(Path(app_path).resolve())
   569→        self.peers_config = peers
   570→        self.base_dir = Path(base_dir) if base_dir else Path(f"/tmp/{name}")
   571→        self.release = release
   572→        self.profiling = profiling
   573→        self.flame_only = flame_only
   574→        self.heaptrack = heaptrack
   575→        self.keep = keep
   576→        self.debug = debug
   577→
   578→        self._tm: Optional[TmuxManager] = None
   579→        self._handles: Dict[str, PeerHandle] = {}
   580→        self._space_id: Optional[str] = None
   581→        self._page_id: Optional[str] = None
   582→
   583→    def peer(self, name: str) -> PeerHandle:
   584→        """Get a PeerHandle by name."""
   585→        if name not in self._handles:
   586→            raise KeyError(f"Peer '{name}' not found. Available: {list(self._handles.keys())}")
   587→        return self._handles[name]
   588→
   589→    @property
   590→    def owner(self) -> PeerHandle:
   591→        """Get the first owner peer."""
   592→        for handle in self._handles.values():
   593→            if handle.role == "owner":
   594→                return handle
   595→        raise RuntimeError("No owner peer configured")
   596→
   597→    @property
   598→    def space_id(self) -> str:
   599→        if self._space_id is None:
   600→            raise RuntimeError("Space not created yet")
   601→        return self._space_id
   602→
   603→    @property
   604→    def page_id(self) -> str:
   605→        if self._page_id is None:
   606→            raise RuntimeError("Page not created yet")
   607→        return self._page_id
   608→
   609→    @staticmethod
   610→    def parse_args(description: str) -> dict:
   611→        """Parse standard CLI args (--keep, --debug, --release).
   612→
   613→        Returns:
   614→            Dict suitable for passing as **kwargs to AppTestScenario().
   615→        """
   616→        parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=description)
   617→        AppTestScenario.add_args(parser)
   618→        args = parser.parse_args()
   619→        return {
   620→            "keep": args.keep,
   621→            "debug": args.debug,
   622→            "release": args.release,
   623→        }
   624→
   625→    @staticmethod
   626→    def add_args(parser: argparse.ArgumentParser) -> None:
   627→        """Add standard flags to an argparse parser."""
   628→        parser.add_argument("--keep", action="store_true",
   629→                            help="Keep tmux session alive after test")
   630→        parser.add_argument("--debug", action="store_true",
   631→                            help="Keep session on failure for debugging")
   632→        parser.add_argument("--release", action="store_true",
   633→                            help="Use release builds")
   634→
   635→    def __enter__(self) -> "AppTestScenario":
   636→        self._setup()
   637→        return self
   638→
   639→    def __exit__(self, exc_type, exc_val, exc_tb):
   640→        if exc_type is not None:
   641→            # Test failed
   642→            print(f"\n[FAIL] {exc_val}")
   643→            traceback.print_exception(exc_type, exc_val, exc_tb)
   644→
   645→            if self.debug:
   646→                self._print_debug_info()
   647→                self._block_until_ctrl_c()
   648→
   649→        if self.keep:
   650→            self._print_session_info()
   651→            self._block_until_ctrl_c()
   652→
   653→        if self._tm:
   654→            self._tm.stop()
   655→
   656→        return exc_type is not None  # Suppress exception if we handled it
   657→
   658→    def _setup(self) -> None:
   659→        """Run the full boilerplate setup."""
   660→        # Determine owner and viewer peers
   661→        owner_name = None
   662→        owner_app = None
   663→        viewer_peers = []
   664→
   665→        for pname, pconfig in self.peers_config.items():
   666→            if pconfig["role"] == "owner" and owner_name is None:
   667→                owner_name = pname
   668→                owner_app = pconfig["app"]
   669→            else:
   670→                viewer_peers.append((pname, pconfig))
   671→
   672→        if owner_name is None:
   673→            raise RuntimeError("At least one peer must have role 'owner'")
   674→
   675→        # 1. Create TmuxManager and add instances
   676→        print(f"\n{'=' * 60}")
   677→        print(f"  {self.name}")
   678→        print(f"{'=' * 60}")
   679→
   680→        self._tm = TmuxManager(
   681→            session_name=self.name,
   682→            base_dir=self.base_dir,
   683→            release=self.release,
   684→            profiling=self.profiling,
   685→            flame_only=self.flame_only,
   686→            heaptrack=self.heaptrack,
   687→        )
   688→        self._tm.add_node("node")
   689→        self._tm.add_shell(owner_name)
   690→        for pname, _ in viewer_peers:
   691→            self._tm.add_shell(pname)
   692→        self._tm.start()
   693→
   694→        node = self._tm.get_client("node")
   695→        owner_client = self._tm.get_client(owner_name)
   696→        print("  All instances ready")
   697→
   698→        # 2. Owner: signup, create space
   699→        print(f"\n  {owner_name}: signup, create space...")
   700→        owner_client.signup_or_login(owner_name)
   701→        space = owner_client.create_space_with_pages(self.app_path)
   702→        self._space_id = space["id"]
   703→
   704→        pages = owner_client.list_pages(self._space_id)
   705→        assert pages, "No pages after create_space_with_pages"
   706→        self._page_id = pages[0]["id"]
   707→        print(f"  Space: {self._space_id[:8]}..., Page: {self._page_id[:8]}...")
   708→
   709→        # 3. Connect to node, publish
   710→        print(f"  {owner_name}: connect to node, publish...")
   711→        owner_client.connect_to_node(node)
   712→        time.sleep(2)
   713→        owner_client.publish_to_node(self._space_id)
   714→        time.sleep(2)
   715→        print("  Published")
   716→
   717→        # 4. Setup each viewer
   718→        for pname, pconfig in viewer_peers:
   719→            viewer_client = self._tm.get_client(pname)
   720→            print(f"  {pname}: signup, subscribe...")
   721→            viewer_client.signup_or_login(pname)
   722→            owner_client.add_viewer(viewer_client, self._space_id)
   723→
   724→            # Wait for viewer to sync space
   725→            viewer_page_id = None
   726→            for i in range(30):
   727→                time.sleep(0.5)
   728→                spaces = viewer_client.list_spaces()
   729→                if spaces:
   730→                    viewer_pages = viewer_client.list_pages(spaces[0]["id"])
   731→                    if viewer_pages:
   732→                        viewer_page_id = viewer_pages[0]["id"]
   733→                        print(f"  {pname} synced in {(i+1)*0.5:.1f}s")
   734→                        break
   735→            if not viewer_page_id:
   736→                raise RuntimeError(f"{pname} failed to sync space")
   737→
   738→        # 5. Open apps on all peers
   739→        print("  Opening apps...")
   740→        owner_client.open_app(self._page_id, owner_app)
   741→        time.sleep(2)
   742→
   743→        for pname, pconfig in viewer_peers:
   744→            viewer_client = self._tm.get_client(pname)
   745→            # Viewer's page_id may differ from owner's
   746→            spaces = viewer_client.list_spaces()
   747→            viewer_pages = viewer_client.list_pages(spaces[0]["id"])
   748→            viewer_page_id = viewer_pages[0]["id"]
   749→            viewer_client.open_app(viewer_page_id, pconfig["app"])
   750→            time.sleep(1)
   751→        print("  All apps opened")
   752→
   753→        # 6. Wait for eval readiness on all peers
   754→        print("  Waiting for eval readiness...")
   755→        for pname in self.peers_config:
   756→            client = self._tm.get_client(pname)
   757→            for i in range(30):
   758→                try:
   759→                    client.eval("return 1")
   760→                    break
   761→                except Exception:
   762→                    time.sleep(0.5)
   763→            else:
   764→                raise RuntimeError(f"{pname} eval not ready after 15s")
   765→
   766→        # 7. Build PeerHandles
   767→        for pname, pconfig in self.peers_config.items():
   768→            client = self._tm.get_client(pname)
   769→            # Resolve viewer page_id
   770→            if pconfig["role"] == "owner":
   771→                peer_page_id = self._page_id
   772→            else:
   773→                spaces = client.list_spaces()
   774→                peer_pages = client.list_pages(spaces[0]["id"])
   775→                peer_page_id = peer_pages[0]["id"]
   776→
   777→            self._handles[pname] = PeerHandle(
   778→                name=pname,
   779→                client=client,
   780→                role=pconfig["role"],
   781→                space_id=self._space_id,
   782→                page_id=peer_page_id,
   783→                app_name=pconfig["app"],
   784→            )
   785→
   786→        print(f"\n  Ready! Peers: {list(self._handles.keys())}")
   787→        print(f"{'=' * 60}\n")
   788→
   789→    def _print_session_info(self) -> None:
   790→        """Print tmux session and socket info."""
   791→        print(f"\n{'=' * 60}")
   792→        print(f"  Session kept alive: tmux attach -t {self.name}")
   793→        print(f"{'=' * 60}")
   794→        print(f"\n  Sockets:")
   795→        for pname in self.peers_config:
   796→            path = self._tm.get_socket_path(pname)
   797→            print(f"    {pname:12s}: {path}")
   798→        node_path = self._tm.get_socket_path("node")
   799→        print(f"    {'node':12s}: {node_path}")
   800→
   801→    def _print_debug_info(self) -> None:
   802→        """Print debug state on failure."""

   804→        print(f"\n  Debug state:")
   805→        for pname in self.peers_config:
   806→            try:
   807→                client = self._tm.get_client(pname)

   809→                print(f"    {pname}: {state}")
   810→            except Exception as e:

   812→
   813→    def _block_until_ctrl_c(self) -> None:

    41→        end
    42→    end
    43→
    44→    -- Sort by timestamp
    45→    table.sort(raw_msgs, function(a, b)
    46→        return (a.timestamp or 0) < (b.timestamp or 0)
    47→    end)
    48→
    49→    -- Transform to UI format
    50→    local ui_msgs = {}
    51→    for _, msg in ipairs(raw_msgs) do
    52→        table.insert(ui_msgs, M.to_ui_message(msg))
    53→    end
    54→
    55→    return ui_msgs
    56→end
    57→
    58→-- Convert raw message to UI Message struct
    59→function M.to_ui_message(msg)
    60→    if not msg then return nil end
    61→    local is_mine = msg.sender_did == my_did
    62→    local reactions = M.transform_reactions(msg.reactions)
    63→
    64→    return {
    65→        id = msg.id or "",
    66→        sender = is_mine and "You" or (msg.sender_name or "???"),
    67→        sender_short = helpers.sender_initials(is_mine and "You" or (msg.sender_name or "?")),
    68→        text = msg.text or "",
    69→        timestamp = helpers.format_time(msg.timestamp),
    70→        is_mine = is_mine,
    71→        deleted = msg.deleted or false,
    72→        edited = msg.edited or false,
    73→        reply_to = msg.reply_to or "",
    74→        reply_preview = msg.reply_preview or "",
    75→        thread_parent_id = msg.thread_parent_id or "",
    76→        thread_reply_count = msg.thread_reply_count or 0,
    77→        reactions = reactions,
    78→        has_attachment = (msg.attachment_hash and msg.attachment_hash ~= "") and true or false,
    79→        attachment_name = msg.attachment_name or "",
    80→    }
    81→end
    82→
    83→-- Transform reactions array: { emoji, users[] } -> { emoji, count, has_mine }
    84→function M.transform_reactions(reactions)
    85→    if not reactions or type(reactions) ~= "table" then return {} end
    86→
    87→    local result = {}
    88→    for _, r in ipairs(reactions) do
    89→        if r.emoji then
    90→            table.insert(result, {
    91→                emoji = r.emoji,
    92→                count = r.users and #r.users or 0,
    93→                has_mine = helpers.contains(r.users, my_did),
    94→            })
    95→        end
    96→    end
    97→    return result
    98→end
    99→
   100→-- Send a new message to the given messages layer
   101→function M.send(messages_layer, text, reply_to_id, reply_preview)
   102→    if not text or text == "" or not messages_layer then return end
   103→
   104→    local msg_id = helpers.generate_id()
   105→    local msg = {

   152→-- Edit message text (only if sender is me)
   153→function M.edit(messages_layer, msg_id, new_text)
   154→    if not messages_layer or not msg_id then return false end
   155→
   156→    local msg = messages_layer:get(msg_id)
   157→    if not msg then return false end
   158→    if msg.sender_did ~= my_did then return false end
   159→
   160→    msg.text = new_text
   161→    msg.edited = true
   162→    messages_layer:set(msg_id, msg)
   163→    return true
   164→end
   165→
   166→-- Soft-delete message (only if sender is me)
   167→function M.delete(messages_layer, msg_id)
   168→    if not messages_layer or not msg_id then return false end
   169→
   170→    local msg = messages_layer:get(msg_id)
   171→    if not msg then return false end
   172→    if msg.sender_did ~= my_did then return false end
   173→
   174→    msg.deleted = true
   175→    messages_layer:set(msg_id, msg)
   176→    return true
   177→end
   178→
   179→-- Toggle reaction on a message
   180→function M.toggle_reaction(messages_layer, msg_id, emoji_char)
   181→    if not messages_layer or not msg_id then return end
   182→
   183→    local msg = messages_layer:get(msg_id)
   184→    if not msg then return end
   185→
   186→    local reactions = msg.reactions or {}
   187→    local found = false
   188→
   189→    for i, reaction in ipairs(reactions) do
   190→        if reaction.emoji == emoji_char then
   191→            found = true
   192→            local user_idx = helpers.find_index(reaction.users, my_did)
   193→            if user_idx then
   194→                table.remove(reaction.users, user_idx)
   195→                if #reaction.users == 0 then
   196→                    table.remove(reactions, i)
   197→                end
   198→            else
   199→                table.insert(reaction.users, my_did)
   200→            end
   201→            break
   202→        end
   203→    end
   204→
   205→    if not found then
   206→        table.insert(reactions, { emoji = emoji_char, users = { my_did } })
   207→    end
   208→
   209→    msg.reactions = reactions
   210→    messages_layer:set(msg_id, msg)
   211→end
   212→
   213→-- Insert emoji character into draft text
   214→function M.insert_emoji_to_draft(emoji_name)
   215→    local shortcode = EMOJI_SHORTCODES[emoji_name]
   216→    local emoji_char = shortcode and emoji:get(shortcode)
   217→    local to_insert = emoji_char or emoji_name
   218→    local current = ui:get("draft_text") or ""
   219→    ui:set("draft_text", current .. to_insert)
   220→end
   221→
   222→-- Resolve emoji name to character
   223→function M.resolve_emoji(emoji_name)
   224→    local shortcode = EMOJI_SHORTCODES[emoji_name]
   225→    return shortcode and emoji:get(shortcode) or emoji_name
   226→end
   227→
   228→-- Get raw message by ID from layer
   229→function M.get_raw(messages_layer, msg_id)
   230→    if not messages_layer or not msg_id then return nil end
   231→    return messages_layer:get(msg_id)
   232→end
   233→
   234→return M

1→-- Threads — open/close thread, send reply
     2→
     3→local helpers = require("ui_helpers")
     4→local messages = require("messages")
     5→
     6→local M = {}
     7→
     8→-- Module state
     9→local my_did = nil
    10→local my_name = nil
    11→local thread_parent_id = nil
    12→
    13→function M.init(did, name)
    14→    my_did = did
    15→    my_name = name
    16→end
    17→
    18→-- Open thread panel for a given message
    19→function M.open(messages_layer, msg_id)
    20→    if not messages_layer or not msg_id then return end
    21→
    22→    local parent_msg = messages_layer:get(msg_id)
    23→    if not parent_msg then return end
    24→
    25→    thread_parent_id = msg_id
    26→
    27→    -- Set parent message in UI
    28→    ui:set("thread_parent", messages.to_ui_message(parent_msg))
    29→    ui:set("thread_open", true)
    30→    ui:set("thread_draft", "")
    31→
    32→    -- Collect thread replies
    33→    M.refresh_replies(messages_layer)
    34→end
    35→
    36→-- Refresh thread replies from layer
    37→function M.refresh_replies(messages_layer)
    38→    if not messages_layer or not thread_parent_id then return end
    39→
    40→    local replies = {}
    41→    local keys = messages_layer:keys()
    42→    if keys then
    43→        for _, key in ipairs(keys) do
    44→            local msg = messages_layer:get(key)
    45→            if msg and msg.thread_parent_id == thread_parent_id then
    46→                table.insert(replies, msg)
    47→            end
    48→        end
    49→    end
    50→
    51→    -- Sort by timestamp
    52→    table.sort(replies, function(a, b)
    53→        return (a.timestamp or 0) < (b.timestamp or 0)
    54→    end)
    55→
    56→    -- Transform to UI format
    57→    local ui_replies = {}
    58→    for _, msg in ipairs(replies) do
    59→        table.insert(ui_replies, messages.to_ui_message(msg))
    60→    end
    61→
    62→    ui:set("thread_messages", ui_replies)
    63→
    64→    -- Also refresh parent (reply count may have changed)
    65→    local parent = messages_layer:get(thread_parent_id)
    66→    if parent then
    67→        ui:set("thread_parent", messages.to_ui_message(parent))
    68→    end
    69→end
    70→
    71→-- Send a reply in the current thread
    72→function M.send_reply(messages_layer)
    73→    if not messages_layer or not thread_parent_id then return end
    74→
    75→    local text = ui:get("thread_draft")
    76→    if not text or text == "" then return end
    77→
    78→    local msg_id = helpers.generate_id()
    79→    local msg = {
    80→        id = msg_id,
    81→        sender_did = my_did,
    82→        sender_name = my_name,
    83→        text = text,
    84→        timestamp = os.time(),
    85→        deleted = false,
    86→        edited = false,
    87→        thread_parent_id = thread_parent_id,
    88→        thread_reply_count = 0,
    89→        reply_to = "",
    90→        reply_preview = "",
    91→        reactions = {},
    92→        attachment_hash = "",
    93→        attachment_name = "",
    94→    }
    95→
    96→    messages_layer:set(msg_id, msg)
    97→
    98→    -- Increment parent's reply count
    99→    local parent = messages_layer:get(thread_parent_id)
   100→    if parent then
   101→        parent.thread_reply_count = (parent.thread_reply_count or 0) + 1
   102→        messages_layer:set(thread_parent_id, parent)
   103→    end
   104→
   105→    ui:set("thread_draft", "")
   106→
   107→    -- Refresh thread view
   108→    M.refresh_replies(messages_layer)
   109→end
   110→
   111→-- Close thread panel
   112→function M.close()
   113→    thread_parent_id = nil
   114→    ui:set("thread_open", false)
   115→    ui:set("thread_messages", {})
   116→    ui:set("thread_draft", "")
   117→end
   118→
   119→-- Check if thread is open
   120→function M.is_open()
   121→    return thread_parent_id ~= nil
   122→end
   123→
   124→-- Get current thread parent ID
   125→function M.get_parent_id()
   126→    return thread_parent_id
   127→end
   128→
   129→return M
   130→

1→-- Read Tracker — local-only read positions and unread/mention detection
     2→
     3→local M = {}
     4→
     5→local page_id, my_did, my_name = nil, nil, nil
     6→local read_positions_layer = nil
     7→
     8→function M.init(pid, did, name)
     9→    page_id = pid
    10→    my_did = did
    11→    my_name = name
    12→    read_positions_layer = scribe:map(page_id .. "/read_positions")
    13→end
    14→
    15→-- Mark channel as read (set last_read to latest msg timestamp)
    16→function M.mark_read(channel_id, messages_layer)
    17→    if not read_positions_layer or not messages_layer then return end
    18→    local latest_ts = 0
    19→    local keys = messages_layer:keys()
    20→    if keys then
    21→        for _, key in ipairs(keys) do
    22→            local msg = messages_layer:get(key)
    23→            if msg and (msg.timestamp or 0) > latest_ts then
    24→                latest_ts = msg.timestamp
    25→            end
    26→        end
    27→    end
    28→    if latest_ts > 0 then
    29→        local my_positions = read_positions_layer:get(my_did) or { channels = {} }
    30→        my_positions.channels[channel_id] = latest_ts
    31→        read_positions_layer:set(my_did, my_positions)
    32→    end
    33→end
    34→
    35→-- Get my last read timestamp for a channel
    36→function M.get_last_read(channel_id)
    37→    if not read_positions_layer then return 0 end
    38→    local my_positions = read_positions_layer:get(my_did)
    39→    if not my_positions or not my_positions.channels then return 0 end
    40→    return my_positions.channels[channel_id] or 0
    41→end
    42→
    43→-- Count unread messages and detect @mentions in a channel
    44→function M.count_unread(channel_id, messages_layer)
    45→    if not messages_layer then return 0, false end
    46→    local last_read = M.get_last_read(channel_id)
    47→    local count = 0
    48→    local has_mention = false
    49→    local keys = messages_layer:keys()
    50→    if keys then
    51→        for _, key in ipairs(keys) do
    52→            local msg = messages_layer:get(key)
    53→            if msg and (msg.timestamp or 0) > last_read
    54→               and (not msg.thread_parent_id or msg.thread_parent_id == "")
    55→               and not msg.deleted then
    56→                count = count + 1
    57→                if msg.text and my_name and msg.text:find("@" .. my_name) then
    58→                    has_mention = true
    59→                end
    60→            end
    61→        end
    62→    end
    63→    return count, has_mention
    64→end
    65→
    66→return M
    67→

1→#!/usr/bin/env python3
     2→"""
     3→Group Chat E2E Test — bidirectional message sync.
     4→
     5→Tests:
     6→- Alice sends message -> syncs to Bob and Carol
     7→- Bob replies -> syncs back to Alice and Carol
     8→
     9→Usage:
    10→    python e2e_tests/test_chat.py
    11→    python e2e_tests/test_chat.py --keep
    12→    python e2e_tests/test_chat.py --debug
    13→"""
    14→
    15→import sys
    16→from pathlib import Path
    17→
    18→sys.path.insert(0, str(Path(__file__).parent.parent / "scripts"))
    19→
    20→from osvauld.scenario import AppTestScenario
    21→
    22→DEMOS_APP = Path(__file__).parent.parent / "sample_apps" / "osvauld-demos"
    23→
    24→args = AppTestScenario.parse_args("Group Chat E2E Test")
    25→
    26→with AppTestScenario(
    27→    name="chat_test",
    28→    app_path=str(DEMOS_APP),
    29→    peers={
    30→        "alice": {"role": "owner", "app": "Group Chat"},
    31→        "bob": {"role": "viewer", "app": "Group Chat"},
    32→        "carol": {"role": "viewer", "app": "Group Chat"},
    33→    },
    34→    **args,
    35→) as s:
    36→    alice = s.peer("alice")
    37→    bob = s.peer("bob")
    38→    carol = s.peer("carol")
    39→
    40→    # Alice sends a message
    41→    print("[1/4] Alice sends message...")
    42→    alice.eval('send_message("Hello from Alice!")')
    43→    alice.wait_for(
    44→        lambda: alice.eval("return get_message_count()") >= 1,
    45→        desc="alice message count",
    46→    )
    47→    print(f"  Alice has {alice.eval('return get_message_count()')} message(s)")
    48→
    49→    # Wait for sync to Bob and Carol
    50→    print("[2/4] Waiting for sync to Bob and Carol...")
    51→    bob.wait_for(
    52→        lambda: bob.eval("return get_message_count()") >= 1,
    53→        desc="Bob messages sync",
    54→    )
    55→    carol.wait_for(
    56→        lambda: carol.eval("return get_message_count()") >= 1,
    57→        desc="Carol messages sync",
    58→    )
    59→    print(f"  Bob has {bob.eval('return get_message_count()')} message(s) - SYNC OK")
    60→    print(f"  Carol has {carol.eval('return get_message_count()')} message(s) - SYNC OK")
    61→
    62→    # Bob replies
    63→    print("[3/4] Bob sends reply...")
    64→    bob.eval('send_message("Hello back from Bob!")')
    65→
    66→    # Wait for sync to Alice and Carol
    67→    print("[4/4] Waiting for sync to Alice and Carol...")
    68→    alice.wait_for(
    69→        lambda: alice.eval("return get_message_count()") >= 2,
    70→        desc="Alice reply sync",
    71→    )
    72→    carol.wait_for(
    73→        lambda: carol.eval("return get_message_count()") >= 2,
    74→        desc="Carol reply sync",
    75→    )
    76→    print(f"  Alice has {alice.eval('return get_message_count()')} message(s) - BIDIRECTIONAL SYNC OK")
    77→    print(f"  Carol has {carol.eval('return get_message_count()')} message(s) - THREE-WAY SYNC OK")
    78→
    79→    print(f"\n{'=' * 60}")
    80→    print("  [SUCCESS] Group Chat E2E Test Passed!")
    81→    print(f"{'=' * 60}")

1→//! Unified Scribe Bindings for Lua
     2→//!
     3→//! Provides a single `scribe` binding that replaces multiple separate bindings (loro, permit, peers).
     4→//! Apps interact with Scribe via this unified API for identity, layers, contacts, and ephemerals.
     5→//!
     6→//! ## API Reference
     7→//!
     8→//! ### Identity
     9→//! - `scribe:my_did()` - Get our DID
    10→//! - `scribe:my_name()` - Get our display name (from permit presence)
    11→//! - `scribe:page_id()` - Get current page ID
    12→//!
    13→//! ### Layers (CRDT)
    14→//! - `scribe:list(name)` - Get or create a list layer
    15→//! - `scribe:map(name)` - Get or create a map layer
    16→//!
    17→//! ### Bindings (Declarative Layer → UI Sync)
    18→//! - `scribe:bind(ui_property, layer_pattern, options?)` - Auto-sync layer to UI
    19→//!
    20→//! ### Contacts
    21→//! - `scribe:get_contacts()` - Get contents of /users layer (persistent contacts)
    22→//!
    23→//! ### Ephemerals
    24→//! - `scribe:send(func, args)` - Send structured ephemeral (permission-validated)
    25→
    26→use mlua::{Error as LuaError, Function, Lua, Result as LuaResult, Table, UserData, UserDataMethods, Value as LuaValue};
    27→use parking_lot::Mutex;
    28→use std::sync::Arc;
    29→use tokio::sync::mpsc;
    30→use tracing::{debug, info, warn};
    31→
    32→use crate::scribe_handle::ScribeHandle;
    33→
    34→use super::binding::{
    35→    expand_pattern, is_wildcard_pattern, process_binding_data, BindingManager, BindingOptions,
    36→};
    37→use super::convert::lua_to_json;
    38→use super::loro::{LuaLoroList, LuaLoroMap};
    39→use crate::ui_types::UiMutation;
    40→
    41→/// Unified Scribe bindings for Lua apps
    42→///
    43→/// Provides identity, layers, contacts, binding, and ephemeral functionality.
    44→pub struct ScribeBindings {
    45→    scribe: Arc<dyn ScribeHandle>,
    46→    page_id: String,
    47→    our_did: String,
    48→    our_name: Option<String>,
    49→    /// Binding manager for declarative layer → UI sync
    50→    binding_manager: Arc<Mutex<BindingManager>>,
    51→    /// UI mutation sender (if UI enabled)
    52→    ui_tx: Option<mpsc::Sender<UiMutation>>,
    53→    /// Whether UI is enabled
    54→    ui_enabled: bool,
    55→}
    56→
    57→impl ScribeBindings {
    58→    /// Create new ScribeBindings (no UI)
    59→    pub fn new(
    60→        scribe: Arc<dyn ScribeHandle>,
    61→        page_id: String,
    62→        our_did: String,
    63→        our_name: Option<String>,
    64→    ) -> Self {
    65→        Self {
    66→            scribe,
    67→            page_id,
    68→            our_did,
    69→            our_name,
    70→            binding_manager: Arc::new(Mutex::new(BindingManager::new())),
    71→            ui_tx: None,
    72→            ui_enabled: false,
    73→        }
    74→    }
    75→
    76→    /// Create ScribeBindings with UI support
    77→    pub fn with_ui(
    78→        scribe: Arc<dyn ScribeHandle>,
    79→        page_id: String,
    80→        our_did: String,
    81→        our_name: Option<String>,
    82→        ui_tx: mpsc::Sender<UiMutation>,
    83→    ) -> Self {
    84→        Self {
    85→            scribe,
    86→            page_id,
    87→            our_did,
    88→            our_name,
    89→            binding_manager: Arc::new(Mutex::new(BindingManager::new())),
    90→            ui_tx: Some(ui_tx),
    91→            ui_enabled: true,
    92→        }
    93→    }
    94→
    95→    /// Get reference to the binding manager
    96→    pub fn binding_manager(&self) -> Arc<Mutex<BindingManager>> {
    97→        self.binding_manager.clone()
    98→    }
    99→}
   100→
   101→impl UserData for ScribeBindings {
   102→    fn add_methods<M: UserDataMethods<Self>>(methods: &mut M) {
   103→
   104→        // Get our DID
   105→        //
   106→        // Returns the DID (Decentralized Identifier) of the current user.
   107→        // This is the unique identifier used in permit patterns and layer names.
   108→        methods.add_method("my_did", |_, this, ()| Ok(this.our_did.clone()));
   109→
   110→        // Get the current page ID
   111→        //
   112→        // Returns the page ID this scribe instance is associated with.
   113→        methods.add_method("page_id", |_, this, ()| Ok(this.page_id.clone()));
   114→
   115→        // Get our display name
   116→        //
   117→        // Returns the display name if available, or nil.
   118→        methods.add_method("my_name", |_, this, ()| {
   119→            Ok(this.our_name.clone())
   120→        });
   121→
   122→        // Send structured ephemeral data
   123→        //
   124→        // Broadcasts ephemeral (non-persistent) data to all peers.
   125→        // Used for typing indicators, cursor positions, game state, etc.
   126→        methods.add_method("send", |_, this, (func, args): (String, LuaValue)| {
   127→            let json_args = lua_to_json(&args)?;
   128→
   129→            let payload = serde_json::json!({
   130→                "func": func,
   131→                "args": json_args,
   132→            });
   133→
   134→            let payload_bytes = serde_json::to_vec(&payload)
   135→                .map_err(|e| LuaError::RuntimeError(format!("Failed to serialize ephemeral: {}", e)))?;
   136→
   137→            this.scribe.send_ephemeral(payload_bytes)
   138→                .map_err(|e| LuaError::RuntimeError(format!("Failed to send ephemeral: {}", e)))?;
   139→
   140→            Ok(())
   141→        });
   142→
   143→        // Create a dynamic layer from a schema pattern
   144→        //
   145→        // Creates a dynamic layer matching a schema defined in the permit's dynamic_layer_schemas.
   146→        // The schema_key identifies the pattern (e.g., "channels/{id}/messages"),
   147→        // and layer_id fills the {id} placeholder (e.g., "general").
   148→        //
   149→        // Returns a table with:
   150→        //   - layer_name: The full layer name (e.g., "{page_id}/channels/{did}/general/messages")
   151→        //
   152→        // # Examples
   153→        // ```lua
   154→        // local result = scribe:create_layer("channels/{id}/messages", "general")
   155→        // print(result.layer_name) -- "page1/channels/did:key:alice/general/messages"
   156→        // local messages = scribe:list(result.layer_name)
   157→        // messages:push({text = "Hello!"})
   158→        // ```
   159→        methods.add_method("create_layer", |lua, this, (schema_key, layer_id): (String, String)| {
   160→            let layer_name = this.scribe.create_layer(&schema_key, &layer_id)
   161→                .map_err(|e| LuaError::RuntimeError(format!("Failed to create dynamic layer: {}", e)))?;
   162→
   163→            let result = lua.create_table()?;
   164→            result.set("layer_name", layer_name)?;
   165→            Ok(result)
   166→        });
   167→
   168→        // Get or create a list layer
   169→        //
   170→        // Returns a handle to the specified list layer, creating it if it doesn't exist.
   171→        // The layer name can include the page_id, e.g., `scribe:list(page_id .. "/messages")`
   172→        methods.add_method("list", |_, this, name: String| {
   173→            this.scribe.ensure_list(&name)
   174→                .map_err(|e| LuaError::RuntimeError(e))?;
   175→            Ok(LuaLoroList::new(this.scribe.clone(), name))
   176→        });
   177→
   178→        // Get or create a map layer
   179→        //
   180→        // Returns a handle to the specified map layer, creating it if it doesn't exist.
   181→        methods.add_method("map", |_, this, name: String| {
   182→            this.scribe.ensure_map(&name)
   183→                .map_err(|e| LuaError::RuntimeError(e))?;
   184→            Ok(LuaLoroMap::new(this.scribe.clone(), name))
   185→        });
   186→
   187→        // List layers matching a pattern
   188→        //
   189→        // Returns a table of layer names matching the glob pattern.
   190→        // Example: scribe:list_layers("*:orders") returns all order layers
   191→        methods.add_method("list_layers", |lua, this, pattern: String| {
   192→            let names = this.scribe.list_layers(&pattern)
   193→                .map_err(|e| LuaError::RuntimeError(e))?;
   194→
   195→            let table = lua.create_table()?;
   196→            for (i, name) in names.iter().enumerate() {
   197→                table.set(i + 1, name.clone())?;
   198→            }
   199→            Ok(table)
   200→        });
   201→
   202→        // Bind a layer pattern to a UI property (declarative sync)
   203→        //
   204→        // Automatically syncs layer data to UI property whenever the layer changes.
   205→        // Supports transform, sort, and filter options.
   206→        //
   207→        // # Arguments
   208→        // * `ui_property` - Name of the UI property/model to sync to
   209→        // * `layer_pattern` - Layer pattern (page_id auto-prepended)
   210→        // * `options` (optional) - Table with transform, sort, filter functions
   211→        //
   212→        // # Placeholders
   213→        // * `{me}` - Expands to user's DID
   214→        //
   215→        // # Examples
   216→        // ```lua
   217→        // -- Simple binding
   218→        // scribe:bind("products", "products")
   219→        //
   220→        // -- With transform and sort
   221→        // scribe:bind("orders", "derived/orders_summary", {
   222→        //     transform = function(item) return {id=item.id, name=item.name} end,
   223→        //     sort = function(a, b) return a.created_at > b.created_at end
   224→        // })
   225→        //
   226→        // -- {me} placeholder
   227→        // scribe:bind("my_orders", "orders/{me}")
   228→        //
   229→        // -- Wildcard (aggregates matching layers)
   230→        // scribe:bind("all_orders", "orders/*")
   231→        // ```
   232→        methods.add_method(
   233→            "bind",
   234→            |lua, this, (ui_property, layer_pattern, options): (String, String, Option<Table>)| {
   235→                if !this.ui_enabled {
   236→                    debug!(
   237→                        ui_property = %ui_property,
   238→                        layer_pattern = %layer_pattern,
   239→                        "scribe:bind() called but UI not enabled, skipping"
   240→                    );
   241→                    return Ok(());
   242→                }
   243→
   244→                // Expand placeholders in pattern
   245→                let expanded_pattern = expand_pattern(&layer_pattern, &this.page_id, &this.our_did);
   246→                let is_wildcard = is_wildcard_pattern(&layer_pattern);
   247→
   248→                info!(
   249→                    ui_property = %ui_property,
   250→                    raw_pattern = %layer_pattern,
   251→                    expanded_pattern = %expanded_pattern,
   252→                    is_wildcard = is_wildcard,
   253→                    "scribe:bind() - registering binding"
   254→                );
   255→
   256→                // Parse options
   257→                // NOTE: sort is NOT supported - sorting is a Slint view concern
   258→                // This enables surgical updates with stable indices
   259→                let binding_options = if let Some(opts) = options {
   260→                    let transform = opts
   261→                        .get::<Function>("transform")
   262→                        .ok()
   263→                        .map(|f| lua.create_registry_value(f))
   264→                        .transpose()
   265→                        .map_err(|e| LuaError::RuntimeError(format!("Failed to store transform: {}", e)))?;

   267→                    let key = opts.get::<String>("key").ok();
   268→                    let max_items = opts.get::<usize>("max_items").ok();

   277→                };

   279→                // Register binding

   281→                    let mut manager = this.binding_manager.lock();

1→"""
     2→Session - Manages a single slint_shell instance
     3→
     4→A Session encapsulates:
     5→- Starting the shell process with control socket
     6→- Waiting for the socket to be ready
     7→- Providing a ControlClient for communication
     8→- Cleanup on exit
     9→"""
    10→
    11→import os
    12→import subprocess
    13→import time
    14→from pathlib import Path
    15→from typing import Optional
    16→
    17→from .client import ControlClient
    18→
    19→
    20→# Default paths
    21→DEFAULT_SHELL_BINARY = Path(__file__).parent.parent.parent / "target" / "debug" / "slint_shell"
    22→
    23→
    24→class Session:
    25→    """Manages a single slint_shell instance."""
    26→
    27→    def __init__(
    28→        self,
    29→        name: str,
    30→        data_dir: str,
    31→        socket_path: Optional[str] = None,
    32→        shell_binary: Optional[Path] = None,
    33→        startup_timeout: float = 5.0,
    34→        show_ui: bool = False,
    35→    ):
    36→        """
    37→        Args:
    38→            name: Instance name (used for logging, display name)
    39→            data_dir: Directory for database storage (STHALAM_DATA_DIR)
    40→            socket_path: Path for control socket (default: {data_dir}/{name}.sock)
    41→            shell_binary: Path to slint_shell binary
    42→            startup_timeout: How long to wait for socket to be ready
    43→            show_ui: If True, don't set SLINT_BACKEND=testing (show actual UI)
    44→        """
    45→        self.name = name
    46→        self.data_dir = data_dir
    47→        self.socket_path = socket_path or f"{data_dir}/{name}.sock"
    48→        self.shell_binary = shell_binary or DEFAULT_SHELL_BINARY
    49→        self.startup_timeout = startup_timeout
    50→        self.show_ui = show_ui
    51→
    52→        self.process: Optional[subprocess.Popen] = None
    53→        self._client: Optional[ControlClient] = None
    54→
    55→    @property
    56→    def client(self) -> ControlClient:
    57→        """Get the ControlClient for this session."""
    58→        if self._client is None:
    59→            raise RuntimeError(f"Session '{self.name}' not started")
    60→        return self._client
    61→
    62→    def start(self) -> "Session":
    63→        """Start the shell process and wait for socket.
    64→
    65→        Returns:
    66→            self (for chaining)
    67→
    68→        Raises:
    69→            FileNotFoundError: If shell binary doesn't exist
    70→            RuntimeError: If shell fails to start or socket not ready in time
    71→        """
    72→        if not self.shell_binary.exists():
    73→            raise FileNotFoundError(
    74→                f"Shell binary not found: {self.shell_binary}\n"
    75→                "Run: cargo build -p slint_shell"
    76→            )
    77→
    78→        # Ensure data directory exists
    79→        os.makedirs(self.data_dir, exist_ok=True)
    80→
    81→        # Clean up stale socket
    82→        if os.path.exists(self.socket_path):
    83→            os.remove(self.socket_path)
    84→
    85→        # Set up environment
    86→        env = os.environ.copy()
    87→        env["STHALAM_DATA_DIR"] = self.data_dir
    88→        if not self.show_ui:
    89→            env["SLINT_BACKEND"] = "testing"
    90→
    91→        # Start process
    92→        self.process = subprocess.Popen(
    93→            [
    94→                str(self.shell_binary),
    95→                "-d", self.name,
    96→                "--debug-socket", self.socket_path,
    97→            ],
    98→            env=env,
    99→            stdout=subprocess.PIPE,
   100→            stderr=subprocess.PIPE,
   101→        )
   102→
   103→        # Wait for socket to be available
   104→        start_time = time.time()
   105→        while time.time() - start_time < self.startup_timeout:
   106→            if os.path.exists(self.socket_path):
   107→                try:
   108→                    client = ControlClient(self.socket_path)
   109→                    if client.ping():
   110→                        self._client = client
   111→                        return self
   112→                except (ConnectionError, RuntimeError):
   113→                    pass
   114→            time.sleep(0.1)
   115→
   116→        # Startup failed
   117→        self.stop()
   118→        raise RuntimeError(
   119→            f"Session '{self.name}' failed to start within {self.startup_timeout}s"
   120→        )
   121→
   122→    def stop(self) -> None:
   123→        """Stop the shell process and clean up."""
   124→        if self.process:
   125→            self.process.terminate()
   126→            try:
   127→                self.process.wait(timeout=2)
   128→            except subprocess.TimeoutExpired:
   129→                self.process.kill()
   130→                self.process.wait()
   131→            self.process = None
   132→
   133→        # Clean up socket
   134→        if os.path.exists(self.socket_path):
   135→            os.remove(self.socket_path)
   136→
   137→        self._client = None
   138→
   139→    def is_running(self) -> bool:
   140→        """Check if the shell process is running."""
   141→        return self.process is not None and self.process.poll() is None
   142→
   143→    # ============================================================
   144→    # Convenience methods (delegate to client)
   145→    # ============================================================
   146→
   147→    def eval(self, code: str):
   148→        """Execute Lua code."""
   149→        return self.client.eval(code)
   150→
   151→    def signup(self, username: str, passphrase: str):
   152→        """Sign up a new user."""
   153→        return self.client.signup(username, passphrase)
   154→
   155→    def login(self, passphrase: str):
   156→        """Login with passphrase."""
   157→        return self.client.login(passphrase)
   158→
   159→    def create_space(self, name: str, template_path: str):
   160→        """Create a space."""
   161→        return self.client.create_space(name, template_path)
   162→
   163→    def import_page(self, space_id: str, page_dir: str):
   164→        """Import a page."""
   165→        return self.client.import_page(space_id, page_dir)
   166→
   167→    def open_app(self, page_id: str, app_name: str):
   168→        """Open an app."""
   169→        return self.client.open_app(page_id, app_name)
   170→
   171→    def list_spaces(self):
   172→        """List spaces."""
   173→        return self.client.list_spaces()
   174→
   175→    def list_pages(self, space_id: str):
   176→        """List pages in a space."""
   177→        return self.client.list_pages(space_id)
   178→
   179→    # ============================================================
   180→    # Context manager support
   181→    # ============================================================
   182→
   183→    def __enter__(self) -> "Session":
   184→        self.start()
   185→        return self
   186→
   187→    def __exit__(self, exc_type, exc_val, exc_tb):
   188→        self.stop()
   189→        return False  # Don't suppress exceptions
   190→

1→//! Scribe message types
     2→//!
     3→//! Contains both the actor messages (ScribeMessage) and shared types
     4→//! (BroadcastPayload, PageUpdate, etc.)
     5→
     6→use std::collections::HashMap;
     7→use std::path::PathBuf;
     8→
     9→use ractor::RpcReplyPort;
    10→use tokio::sync::mpsc;
    11→use serde::{Serialize, Deserialize};
    12→
    13→use domains::{QuerySpec, QueryDelta, QueryResult, JsonOp};
    14→use crate::Result;
    15→
    16→/// Payload sent to PeerActor for broadcast (3-step sync protocol)
    17→///
    18→/// **Context**: Scribe sends this to PeerActor, who then sends SyncOffer to peer
    19→/// **state_vector**: Our state vector after this update (for 3-step protocol)
    20→/// **layer_type**: Protocol routing hint (App=snapshot, Data=incremental, Static=blob)
    21→#[derive(Debug, Clone)]
    22→pub struct BroadcastPayload {
    23→    pub page_id: String,
    24→    pub layer_name: String,
    25→    pub update: Vec<u8>,
    26→    /// Our state vector for this layer (for SyncOffer message)
    27→    pub state_vector: Vec<u8>,
    28→    /// Layer type for protocol routing
    29→    pub layer_type: domains::LayerType,
    30→}
    31→
    32→/// Ephemeral broadcast payload (generic)
    33→///
    34→/// **Context**: Scribe sends this to Butler/Courier for datagram broadcast
    35→/// **Transport**: Unreliable QUIC datagram (fire-and-forget, lowest latency)
    36→/// **Design**: Generic payload - app defines format; protocol routes by page_id
    37→#[derive(Debug, Clone, serde::Serialize, serde::Deserialize)]
    38→pub struct EphemeralBroadcast {
    39→    /// Page ID for routing
    40→    pub page_id: String,
    41→    /// Opaque payload - app defines format (JSON with type/x/y, etc.)
    42→    pub payload: Vec<u8>,
    43→}
    44→
    45→/// Outbound ephemeral data (Scribe → PeerActor via channel)
    46→///
    47→/// **Context**: Same pattern as BroadcastPayload for CRDT data
    48→/// **Flow**: Scribe broadcasts ephemeral to all subscriber channels,
    49→///           PeerActor listener receives and sends datagram to peer
    50→#[derive(Debug, Clone)]
    51→pub struct EphemeralOutbound {
    52→    /// Page ID for routing (used in datagram)
    53→    pub page_id: String,
    54→    /// Opaque payload - app defines format (JSON with type/x/y, etc.)
    55→    pub payload: Vec<u8>,
    56→}
    57→
    58→/// Delta operations for different Loro container types
    59→///
    60→/// **Context**: Represents incremental changes to CRDT containers
    61→/// **Usage**: Lua apps can apply deltas for efficient UI updates (preserve scroll, animations)
    62→#[derive(Debug, Clone, Serialize, Deserialize)]
    63→#[serde(tag = "type")]
    64→pub enum LoroDelta {
    65→    /// List delta: sequence of Retain/Insert/Delete operations
    66→    List { ops: Vec<ListOp> },
    67→
    68→    /// Map delta: updated keys
    69→    Map { updated: HashMap<String, Option<serde_json::Value>> },
    70→
    71→    /// Text delta (for future rich text support)
    72→    Text { ops: Vec<TextOp> },
    73→}
    74→
    75→/// List delta operations (applied sequentially)
    76→///
    77→/// **Context**: Represents changes to a Loro list container
    78→/// **Example**: [Retain(3), Insert([msg4]), Delete(1)] means "skip 3 items, insert msg4, delete 1 item"
    79→#[derive(Debug, Clone, Serialize, Deserialize)]
    80→#[serde(tag = "op")]
    81→pub enum ListOp {
    82→    /// Keep N items unchanged (advance cursor)
    83→    Retain { count: usize },
    84→
    85→    /// Insert values at current position
    86→    Insert { values: Vec<serde_json::Value> },
    87→
    88→    /// Delete N items at current position
    89→    Delete { count: usize },
    90→}
    91→
    92→/// Text delta operations (for rich text editing)
    93→///
    94→/// **Context**: Represents changes to a Loro text container
    95→/// **Note**: Deferred for now - will implement when we need rich text editing
    96→#[derive(Debug, Clone, Serialize, Deserialize)]
    97→#[serde(tag = "op")]
    98→pub enum TextOp {
    99→    /// Keep N characters unchanged
   100→    Retain { count: usize },
   101→
   102→    /// Insert text at current position
   103→    Insert { text: String },
   104→
   105→    /// Delete N characters at current position
   106→    Delete { count: usize },
   107→}
   108→
   109→// Unified Page Update Channel (Replaces PageEvent + EphemeralEvent + QueryDelta)
   110→
   111→/// Unified update enum for all page events
   112→///
   113→/// **Context**: Single channel replaces 3 separate broadcast types
   114→/// **Benefits**: 3 listener tasks → 1, unified fan-out logic
   115→/// **Consumers**: UI/Lua callbacks, Broadcast to peers, Derivation engine
   116→#[derive(Debug, Clone)]
   117→pub enum PageUpdate {
   118→    /// Layer data changed (local edit or remote sync)
   119→    LayerChanged {
   120→        layer: String,
   121→        from_peer: Option<(String, String)>,  // (did, device_id)
   122→        /// Structured operations extracted from the update (same format as validation)
   123→        /// Enables surgical UI updates - Lua can process individual ops
   124→        ops: Option<Vec<JsonOp>>,
   125→        delta: Option<LoroDelta>,
   126→        state_vector: Vec<u8>,
   127→        /// Full layer state as JSON — None when delta is available (avoids O(N) serialization)
   128→        /// Some for initial load, wildcard bindings, or fallback scenarios
   129→        full_data: Option<serde_json::Value>,
   130→        /// True if this is a newly created layer (first time seeing it)
   131→        created: bool,
   132→    },
   133→
   134→    /// Ephemeral data from remote peer (cursor, typing, etc.)
   135→    Ephemeral {
   136→        user_did: String,
   137→        device_id: String,
   138→        payload: Vec<u8>,
   139→    },
   140→
   141→    /// Query result changed
   142→    QueryUpdated {
   143→        query_id: String,
   144→        delta: QueryDelta,
   145→    },
   146→
   147→    /// Peer subscribed to this page
   148→    PeerSubscribed {
   149→        did: String,
   150→        /// Username if presence.share_username is true in their permit
   151→        username: Option<String>,
   152→    },
   153→
   154→    /// Peer unsubscribed from this page
   155→    PeerUnsubscribed {
   156→        did: String,
   157→    },
   158→
   159→    /// Structured ephemeral received (permission-validated)
   160→    ///
   161→    /// **Context**: Ephemeral with func name, validated against permit
   162→    StructuredEphemeral {
   163→        from_did: String,
   164→        func: String,
   165→        args: serde_json::Value,
   166→    },
   167→}
   168→
   169→/// Type alias for unified page update channel
   170→pub type PageUpdateTx = mpsc::Sender<PageUpdate>;
   171→
   172→/// Events emitted for sync coordination (consumed by Coordinator)
   173→///
   174→/// **Context**: Scribe emits these when it needs to sync with a user.
   175→/// NOTE: Scribe only knows user_did. Coordinator handles everything else:
   176→/// - Device resolution
   177→/// - Connection establishment
   178→/// - Subscription (PeerActor discovers active Scribes on connect)
   179→#[derive(Debug, Clone)]
   180→pub enum SyncEvent {
   181→    /// Ensure this user is synced (connected + subscribed to active Scribes)
   182→    EnsureSync { user_did: String },
   183→
   184→    /// Node detected a new dynamic layer — permits already created by layer_unit
   185→    ///
   186→    /// **Context**: Scribe detected a dynamic layer (via schema match) and used
   187→    /// PermitIssuer to create ready-to-send permits. Coordinator just distributes.
   188→    NewDynamicLayer {
   189→        page_id: String,
   190→        layer_name: String,
   191→        /// Ready-to-send permits: (recipient_did, layer_permit_token)
   192→        permits: Vec<(String, String)>,
   193→    },
   194→}
   195→
   196→// ScribeMessage - Actor Messages for Scribe
   197→
   198→/// Messages received by Scribe actor
   199→#[derive(Debug)]
   200→pub enum ScribeMessage {

Perfect! Now I have a comprehensive understanding of the osvauld-demos app. Let me create a detailed report:

## Exploration Report: osvauld-demos Sample App

### 1. **Lua App Code Structure**

The **Group Chat** app is the primary demo, with a well-organized Lua module architecture:

**Core Files:**
- **`app.lua`** (434 lines) - Main entry point and routing
  - On-init: identity setup, module initialization, layer binding
  - on_click: channel switching, thread operations, reactions, emoji picker, message CRUD
  - on_submit: message sending with reply support, edit detection
  - on_text_input: typing indicators (ephemeral)
  - Exports API: send_message, switch_channel, get_active_channel, get_message_count
  - Uses timer for periodic typing indicator cleanup

- **`channels.lua`** (216 lines) - Channel management
  - State: page_id, my_did, my_name, channels_meta_layer, active_channel, messages_layer
  - `M.init()`: initializes channels_meta layer, ensures defaults (general/random/dev), switches to general
  - `M.ensure_default_channels()`: Creates 3 static channels (no create_layer needed)
  - `M.create_channel(name)`: **Uses `scribe:create_layer("channels/{id}/messages", id)` for custom channels**
    - Sanitizes name (lowercase, replace spaces with hyphens)
    - Calls create_layer → returns full layer_name with page_id prefix
    - Strips page_id prefix, stores bare layer_path in channels_meta
    - Switches to new channel
  - `M.switch_channel()`: Updates UI, rebinds messages layer
  - Implements get_channel_layer_path() which returns static paths for defaults, reads DID-namespaced paths from meta for custom

- **`messages.lua`** (235 lines) - Message operations
  - Transform, send, edit, delete, reactions
  - `M.send()`: Creates message struct with id, sender_did, sender_name, timestamp, text, reply_to, reactions, attachments
  - `M.toggle_reaction()`: Updates reactions array on message
  - Thread support: filters via thread_parent_id, tracks thread_reply_count
  - Soft-delete via deleted flag

- **`threads.lua`** (130 lines) - Thread panel operations
  - `M.open()`: Sets thread_parent_id, fetches parent message
  - `M.refresh_replies()`: Collects all messages with matching thread_parent_id, sorts by timestamp
  - `M.send_reply()`: Creates reply with thread_parent_id set, increments parent's thread_reply_count

- **`read_tracker.lua`** (67 lines) - Local read position tracking
  - `M.mark_read()`: Stores latest message timestamp per channel in read_positions layer
  - `M.count_unread()`: Counts messages after last_read, detects @mentions

- **`ui_helpers.lua`** (48 lines) - Utility functions
  - ID generation, time formatting, text truncation, table operations, sender initials for avatars

### 2. **Permit Template Analysis**

**File**: `/home/abe/osvauld/sample_apps/osvauld-demos/permit_template.json` (633 lines)

**Dynamic Layer Schemas (single schema, "role" grant):**
```json
"dynamic_layer_schemas": {
    "channels/{id}/messages": {
        "type": "map",
        "grant": "role",
        "role_permissions": {
            "owner": { "sync": true, "write": true },
            "collaborator": { "sync": true, "write": true },
            "node": { "sync": true, "write": true }
        }
    }
}
```

**Key Facts:**
- **Grant type: "role"** — not "explicit"
- All peers with matching relationship (owner/collaborator/node) get automatic access
- No creator-only or participant-specific layers implemented
- Static channels (general/random/dev) hardcoded in permit_template.json layers section
- Custom channels created via create_layer() get DID-namespaced layer names
- Schema is replicated at all permission levels: owner_template, node, viewer, collaborator

**Comparison with my-shop app:**
- **my-shop uses "explicit" grant** for orders/{id}:
  ```json
  "grant": "explicit",
  "permissions": { "sync": true, "write": true }
  ```
- Explicit: creator-only access by default; other users need explicit permission (Phase 2d future work per dynamic.rs comments)
- No role_permissions needed for explicit grant

### 3. **How create_layer is Currently Used**

**Flow in channels.lua:**
```lua
local result = scribe:create_layer("channels/{id}/messages", id)
-- Returns: { layer_name = "page_id/channels/did:key:xxx/channel_name/messages" }
```

**Scribe Implementation** (scribe/src/layer_unit/dynamic.rs):
1. Validates schema exists in permit's dynamic_layer_schemas
2. Generates path: `channels/{our_did}/{layer_id}/messages`
3. Creates empty LayerUnit, sets up observer
4. Returns full name with page_id prefix
5. **No automatic permits issued** — role-based access handled by butler/gurkha

**Dynamic Path Generation:**
```rust
fn generate_dynamic_path(schema_key, our_did, layer_id):
    // Schema: "channels/{id}/messages"
    // Input: did:key:alice, "general"
    // Output: "channels/did:key:alice/general/messages"
```

The creator's DID becomes the second segment (namespace), preventing namespace forgery.

### 4. **Slint UI Structure for Group Chat**

**Architecture**: 3-column fixed layout (220px sidebar | flexible main | 350px thread panel)

**Components:**

**`app.slint`** - Main app layout
- **Global AppAPI**: 30+ properties binding Lua data to UI
  - channels, active_channel, messages, thread_*, typing_text
  - draft_text, replying_to_id, show_emoji_picker, auto_scroll
  - show_create_channel, sidebar collapse states
  - Callbacks: on_click, on_submit, on_text_input, pick-asset-file

- **Layout**:
  - Column 1: Sidebar (channel list + online users)
  - Column 2: Messages area (Flickable with Retain scroll target)
    - Header: channel name + topic + auto-scroll toggle
    - Messages Flickable with typing indicator
    - Composer (text input + attachment + emoji buttons)
    - Emoji picker (above composer)
  - Column 3: Thread panel (optional, 350px wide when open)

**`sidebar.slint`** - Channel + user list
- ChannelItem: Shows #name, unread count badge, @mention badge (red), active highlight
- UserItem: Online dot (green for online), username
- Header: workspace name + create channel button
- Scrollable Flickable for channels and users

**`composer.slint`** - Message input
- Reply indicator: Shows "Replying to: [text]" with cancel button
- Attachment button (+)
- Text input with placeholder
- Emoji button (:))
- Send button (implied)
- Reply state adjusts composer height (57px → 93px)

**`message_bubble.slint`** - Message display
- Avatar with initials
- Sender name + timestamp
- Text content with markdown/formatting
- Reactions bar (emoji + count)
- Context menu (reply, thread, edit, delete)

**`thread_panel.slint`** - Right sidebar for threads
- Parent message display (read-only)
- Reply count
- List of threaded replies
- Reply composer at bottom

**`emoji_picker.slint`** - Modal above composer
- 220px tall when visible
- Grid of emoji buttons
- Close button

**Other Slint files:**
- `theme.slint`: Color/font definitions
- `message_bubble.slint`: Message display with reactions
- `thread_panel.slint`: Right panel for threads
- `emoji_picker.slint`: Emoji selection grid

### 5. **No Existing DM or Explicit-Layer Functionality**

**Current Limitations:**
- ✗ No DM/direct message layers
- ✗ No explicit grant schema (only "role" grant for channels)
- ✗ No UI for selecting DM recipients
- ✗ No participant-specific layer access control
- ✗ All created channels use role-based access (owner/collaborator/node relationships)

**What Would Be Needed for DMs:**
1. Add `dms/{id}/messages` schema with `grant: "explicit"` to permit_template.json
2. Create DM creation UI (select recipient dropdown)
3. Lua: `scribe:create_layer("dms/{id}/messages", recipient_did)`
4. Store DM metadata (participants) in a dms_meta layer
5. Add DM panel to sidebar (separate from channel list)
6. Future: implement explicit participant granting (Phase 2d per scribe/src/layer_unit/dynamic.rs comment at line 164)

**Grant Type Comparison:**
- **role-based** (current): All connected peers with matching role get auto-access
- **explicit** (future): Creator-only by default; creator must explicitly grant other participants access
  - In my-shop: orders/{id} uses explicit for order privacy
  - Layer permit currently auto-issued only to creator (line 144-162 in dynamic.rs)
  - TODO comment at line 164: "Named participants (from layer metadata) — Phase 2d"

### 6. **Key Architecture Insights**

**Binding System** (scribe:bind in app.lua):
- Declarative layer → UI property sync
- Supports transform, sort, filter
- Wildcard patterns (*) aggregate multiple layers
- Automatic rebinding on channel switch

**Ephemeral Data** (scribe:send):
- Used for typing indicators: `scribe:send("typing", { user = my_name, channel = id })`
- Validated against permit ephemeral_funcs list
- Unreliable QUIC datagrams, fire-and-forget

**Layer Path Strategy:**
- Static layers: `{page_id}/channels/general/messages` (in permit)
- Dynamic layers: `{page_id}/channels/{creator_did}/{id}/messages` (namespace security)
- Default channels created at init time without create_layer
- Custom channels use create_layer with schema validation

**Message Data Model:**
```lua
{
    id, sender_did, sender_name, text, timestamp,
    deleted, edited, thread_parent_id, thread_reply_count,
    reply_to, reply_preview,
    reactions: [{ emoji, users: [did1, did2] }],
    attachment_hash, attachment_name
}
```

**Read Tracking:**
- Local-only (read_positions layer)
- Per-channel last_read timestamp
- Unread count + @mention detection
- Badges show on inactive channels

This comprehensive exploration reveals a well-structured sample app demonstrating core osvauld patterns: dynamic layers, role-based access, binding system, ephemeral data, and modular Lua architecture. The explicit grant type and DM functionality represent Phase 2d future work.

-- Channels — switch, create, ensure defaults
-- Default channels (general/random/dev) are static layers in the permit template.
-- Custom user-created channels use create_layer() for DID-namespaced dynamic layers.

local M = {}

-- Module state (set by init)
local page_id = nil
local my_did = nil
local my_name = nil
local channels_meta_layer = nil
local active_channel = "general"

-- Current channel's messages layer (LoroMap)
local messages_layer = nil

-- Current channel's bare layer path (for binding/rebinding)
local active_layer_path = nil

-- Callback to refresh messages when channel changes
local on_channel_switch = nil

-- Read tracker module reference (set by init)
local read_tracker = nil

-- Default channels — these are static layers in the permit template
local DEFAULT_CHANNELS = {
    { id = "general", name = "general", topic = "General discussion" },
    { id = "random", name = "random", topic = "Random stuff" },
    { id = "dev", name = "dev", topic = "Development talk" },
}

-- Check if a channel ID is a default (static) channel
local function is_default_channel(channel_id)
    for _, ch in ipairs(DEFAULT_CHANNELS) do
        if ch.id == channel_id then return true end
    end
    return false
end

-- Get the layer path for a channel.
-- Default channels: simple static path (e.g., "channels/general/messages")
-- Custom channels: DID-namespaced path stored in channels_meta
local function get_channel_layer_path(channel_id)
    if is_default_channel(channel_id) then
        return "channels/" .. channel_id .. "/messages"
    end
    -- Custom channel: read DID-namespaced path from meta
    local ch_meta = channels_meta_layer and channels_meta_layer:get(channel_id)
    if ch_meta and ch_meta.layer_path then
        return ch_meta.layer_path
    end
    -- Fallback for channels without stored path
    return "channels/" .. channel_id .. "/messages"
end

function M.init(pid, did, name, callback, tracker)
    page_id = pid
    my_did = did
    my_name = name
    on_channel_switch = callback
    read_tracker = tracker

    channels_meta_layer = scribe:map(page_id .. "/channels_meta")

    M.ensure_default_channels()
    M.switch_channel("general")
end

function M.ensure_default_channels()
    if not channels_meta_layer then return end

    for _, ch in ipairs(DEFAULT_CHANNELS) do
        local existing = channels_meta_layer:get(ch.id)
        if not existing then
            -- Default channels use simple static paths (no create_layer needed)
            channels_meta_layer:set(ch.id, {
                id = ch.id,
                name = ch.name,
                topic = ch.topic,
                created_by = my_did,
                created_at = os.time(),
            })
        end
    end

    M.refresh_channel_list()
end

function M.refresh_channel_list()
    if not channels_meta_layer then return end

    local channel_list = {}
    local keys = channels_meta_layer:keys()
    if keys then
        for _, key in ipairs(keys) do
            local ch = channels_meta_layer:get(key)
            if ch then
                local ch_id = ch.id or key
                local unread = 0
                local has_mention = false
                if read_tracker then
                    local ch_layer_path = get_channel_layer_path(ch_id)
                    local ch_msgs_layer = scribe:map(page_id .. "/" .. ch_layer_path)
                    unread, has_mention = read_tracker.count_unread(ch_id, ch_msgs_layer)
                end
                local is_active = ch_id == active_channel
                table.insert(channel_list, {
                    id = ch_id,
                    name = ch.name or key,
                    topic = ch.topic or "",
                    unread = is_active and 0 or unread,
                    is_active = is_active,
                    has_mention = is_active and false or has_mention,
                })
            end
        end
    end

    -- Sort alphabetically, but keep "general" first
    table.sort(channel_list, function(a, b)
        if a.id == "general" then return true end
        if b.id == "general" then return false end
        return a.name < b.name
    end)

    ui:set("channels", channel_list)
end

function M.switch_channel(channel_id)
    active_channel = channel_id

    local layer_path = get_channel_layer_path(channel_id)
    active_layer_path = layer_path

    -- Get messages layer using the full path
    messages_layer = scribe:map(page_id .. "/" .. layer_path)

    -- Mark as read immediately on switch
    if read_tracker then
        read_tracker.mark_read(channel_id, messages_layer)
    end

    -- Update UI
    local ch_meta = channels_meta_layer and channels_meta_layer:get(channel_id)
    ui:set("active_channel", channel_id)
    ui:set("active_channel_topic", ch_meta and ch_meta.topic or "")

    -- Refresh channel list (to update active state)
    M.refresh_channel_list()

    -- Notify parent with layer_path (for binding/rebinding)
    if on_channel_switch then
        on_channel_switch(channel_id, layer_path)
    end
end

function M.create_channel(name)
    if not name or name == "" then return end
    if not channels_meta_layer then return end

    -- Sanitize: lowercase, replace spaces with hyphens
    local id = name:lower():gsub("%s+", "-"):gsub("[^%w%-]", "")
    if id == "" then return end

    -- Check if already exists
    local existing = channels_meta_layer:get(id)
    if existing then
        M.switch_channel(id)
        return
    end

    -- Custom channels use create_layer() for DID-namespaced dynamic path
    local result = scribe:create_layer("channels/{id}/messages", id)
    local layer_path = nil
    if result and result.layer_name then
        -- Strip page_id/ prefix to get bare path
        local prefix = page_id .. "/"
        if result.layer_name:sub(1, #prefix) == prefix then
            layer_path = result.layer_name:sub(#prefix + 1)
        else
            layer_path = result.layer_name
        end
    end

    channels_meta_layer:set(id, {
        id = id,
        name = id,
        topic = "",
        created_by = my_did,
        created_at = os.time(),
        layer_path = layer_path,
    })

    M.refresh_channel_list()
    M.switch_channel(id)
end

function M.get_active_channel()
    return active_channel
end

function M.get_active_layer_path()
    return active_layer_path
end

function M.get_messages_layer()
    return messages_layer
end

function M.get_channels_meta_layer()
    return channels_meta_layer
end

return M
